test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 27 Feb 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Article 43 B in Part Ⅳ of the Constitution of India deals with:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Cooperative societies**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 43B in Part IV of the Constitution of India explicitly deals with the **promotion of cooperative societies**.
 
• It mandates the state to promote **voluntary formation, autonomous functioning, democratic control, and professional management** of cooperative societies.
 
• This article falls under the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP), which are non-justiciable but aim to guide the state in formulating policies and laws.
 
• The inclusion of Article 43B was brought about by the **97th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2011**, highlighting the importance of cooperatives in the Indian economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**

 
 
• The Directive Principles are guidelines or principles given to the federal institutes governing the state of India, to be kept in citation while framing laws and policies.
 
• They are non-justiciable in nature, meaning they are not enforceable by any court for their violation.
 
• The main aim of DPSPs is to create social and economic conditions under which the citizens can lead a good life.
 
• They also aim to establish social and economic democracy through a welfare state.
 
 
 
• **97th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2011**
 
 
• This amendment added a new Part IXB to the Constitution, which is dedicated to cooperative societies.
 
• It aims to encourage economic activities of cooperatives which in turn help progress rural India.
 
• It also made the right to form cooperative societies a fundamental right under Article 19(1)(c).
 
• This amendment also inserted Article 43B in the DPSPs to ensure the promotion of cooperatives.
 
 
 
• **Cooperative Societies in India**
 
 
• Cooperative societies are voluntary associations of individuals having common needs who combine forces for the achievement of common economic interests.
 
• They play a significant role in the socioeconomic development of the country, especially in rural areas.
 
• Examples include agricultural cooperatives, consumer cooperatives, housing cooperatives, and many more.
 
• The Indian government has been actively promoting cooperative societies through various schemes and legislative measures to enhance their functioning and management.
